title: Choroidal Melanoma: Clinical Mastery & The COMS Legacy
summary: Choroidal melanoma remains the most common primary intraocular malignancy in adults, requiring a nuanced, evidence-based approach to globe-sparing treatment and systemic monitoring. This infographic synthesizes decades of oncology data, primarily from the landmark Collaborative Ocular Melanoma Study (COMS).

sections.title: Definition & Overview
sections.content: Choroidal melanoma arises from uveal melanocytes. It is a highly aggressive tumor with a high propensity for hepatic metastasis. The diagnosis is clinical, often relying on the 'TFSOM-UHHD' criteria. Mortality is primarily determined by hematogenous spread, despite successful local globe-sparing therapy.

sections.title: Management Algorithm
content: Step 1: Multimodal imaging (Fundus photo, B-scan, UBM, OCT, FFA/ICGA).
Step 2: Systemic staging (Liver function tests, abdominal MRI/USG).
Step 3: Choice of local control: Plaque Brachytherapy (I-125, Ru-106, Pd-103) vs. Proton Beam Radiotherapy.
Step 4: Surgical excision for iris/ciliary body involvement if feasible.
Step 5: Regular monitoring for local recurrence and systemic hepatic metastasis.

sections.title: Recent Advances & Landmark Evidence
content: Gene Expression Profiling (GEP): Class 1 (Low risk) vs. Class 2 (High metastatic risk).
PRAME expression as a secondary prognostic marker.
Tezepelumab/Tebentafusp: The first FDA-approved treatment for metastatic uveal melanoma (HLA-A*02:01 positive).
The shift towards personalized medicine using biopsy-driven prognostic testing.
